correctness.rationale: The positive-definite \(m+1\)-hat Gram matrix and Sherman--Morrison inverse are exact; every kernel integral includes the boundary atom. Explicit positive-coefficient polynomials prove strict dominance, positive coefficients of the derivative numerator prove strict monotonicity for every integer \(m\ge2\) and \(w>0\); strict kernel-sign disagreement establishes all norming locations. The \(m=2\) cubic and limits follow algebraically. Symbolic expressions and 63 independently assembled rational Gram cases were executed from the packaged checker. Finite cases do not replace universal proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement pertains to an equilateral metric star with one *outer-leaf* positive Dirac mass, and identifies a strict upward norm perturbation, a relocation of norming points to the other leaves, a unique two-arm threshold, and exact positivity defect. A known star formula without atoms and a hub-atom variant are different measure supports; their conclusions do not imply the new leaf-atom rational norm. Primary full-text comparison gives unrelated or substantially broader estimates, not a covering identity. Unindexed equivalents remain possible.

value.rationale: The exact L-infinity norm of a canonical metric-star finite-element least-squares operator is a natural endpoint stability invariant. A single atomic observation increases worst-case amplification while moving all extremizing locations to unobserved branches, a structural nonlocal effect. The theorem classifies every positive mass and arm count, identifies a unique two-arm crossing of the reference level 2, gives strict monotonicity and limiting laws, and supplies equality/positivity witnesses. These are motivated spectral and approximation-theoretic facts, not an arbitrary finite lookup.
